clips.title: The story
paras: In Razor Hill, Tai'jin sends new priests to prove their healing in the field. They seek Grunt Kor'ja, wounded while standing against Kul Tiras survivors, and tend her injuries. Those who succeed earn ceremonial vestments and recognition among the Horde's spiritual practitioners.

South of Razor Hill, the Horde still fights remnants of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's forces. Tai'jin, the troll priest trainer, tests new priests in the work of real combat triage. She sends them to find Grunt Kor'ja, a warrior badly wounded while repelling human infiltrators. You tend her injuries and strengthen her before she succumbs.

Healing Kor'ja proves a young priest is ready to serve the Horde's spiritual tradition. Tai'jin awards the Garments of Spirituality for saving a frontline defender. To orcs and Darkspear trolls alike, the robes mark their wearer as more than an apprentice of incantations: they can be trusted to keep Horde warriors alive in battle.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: You be ready for your first test, friend. South of Razor Hill, just outta town, one of our grunts be hurt fightin' off some o' Proudmoore's old troops. She not doin' too well, an' she benefit much if one of our kind could help her. Find her—her name be Kor'ja—heal her wounds, an' give her the blessin' of our ancestors.
You do this, an' me thinks that be sufficient proof that you ready to move on in our ways.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Most think it logical that healin' magics be powerful, but not many understand how powerful. You can keep many alive when instead they should be meetin' their own ancestors. This healin' magic mixed with the ability of Fortitude are a very powerful combination of spells. You remember this. It helpful to all manner of people: warriors, mages and everything in between.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Good, then Kor'ja lives and goes off to defend our town from those malicious humans. I often wish to remember days of battle; where power was shown in combat and it was the wise who often destroyed those who relied on just their strength.
You done good by me, friend. You take this robe now. Maybe it help, maybe you not care, but you earned it and I'm proud to call you friend.

sources.title: Quest text as quoted on the Warcraft Wiki
